What changed in medfit 0.11.0 and 0.11.1

Source: vignettes/articles/whats-new-0-11.qmd

This is a practical guide to the changes recorded in NEWS. The native engine’s public interface graduated from experimental status in 0.11.0; the later fixes improve the reliability and interpretation of its results. Examples use the bundled mediation_demo data. Native fits are marked eval: false because optimization can take longer than a quick site build.

Reproducible bootstrap resamples (0.11.1)

What: Nonparametric row and cluster resample indices are drawn in the calling R process before refits are sent to workers. Why: A fixed seed now selects the same resamples and boot_estimates regardless of ncores. Sequential statistics that do not draw random numbers retain the 0.11.0 stream. A statistic that draws its own random numbers is outside this guarantee; its sequential stream changes because those draws follow all resample draws. The pre-drawn indices also use memory proportional to the number of rows times the number of replicates. See R/bootstrap.R.

library(medfit)

Attaching package: 'medfit'
The following object is masked from 'package:stats':

    decompose
stat <- function(d) mean(d$mediator1)
a <- bootstrap_mediation(stat, method = "nonparametric",
                         data = mediation_demo, n_boot = 12, seed = 41)
b <- bootstrap_mediation(stat, method = "nonparametric",
                         data = mediation_demo, n_boot = 12, seed = 41,
                         parallel = TRUE, ncores = 2)
identical(a@boot_estimates, b@boot_estimates)
[1] TRUE

For cluster resampling, pass cluster = "school" on data with a school column. Each draw gets a new cluster ID, including repeated draws of one school.

Interpretable model comparisons (0.11.1)

What: anova() attaches a named logical p_valid attribute. Its first row is NA; a test whose null lies on a boundary is FALSE. The printed p-value and boundary warning remain, but the usual chi-square reference is invalid there. Why: Programs can check validity without parsing a warning. It also refuses pairs with a nonzero fixed parameter on one side and an absent row on the other: those models are not nested. Fixing a parameter that was free in the larger model remains a valid restriction. See R/sem-anova.R.

base <- "mediator1 ~ a*treatment\noutcome ~ b*mediator1 + cp*treatment"
full <- fit_sem(base, mediation_demo)
restricted <- fit_sem(paste(base, "a == 0", sep = "\n"), mediation_demo)
comparison <- anova(full, restricted)
attr(comparison, "p_valid")
# The covariance is fixed at 0.5 in one model but absent (zero) in the other.
with_fixed_covariance <- fit_sem(
  paste(base, "mediator1 ~~ 0.5*outcome", "a == 0", sep = "\n"),
  mediation_demo)
try(anova(full, with_fixed_covariance))

Optimum diagnostics (0.11.1)

What: SEMFit@diagnostics$optimum records n_starts, n_accepted, best_of, certified, spread, and status. Why: A nonlinear constraint can have several feasible branches. The engine tries every start, keeps the lowest discrepancy among accepted solutions, and warns when accepted starts disagree or only one succeeds. certified means a feasible unconstrained reference provides a lower bound attained by the constrained fit; otherwise status can be single, disagreed, or agreed. An ordinary fit reports unique. spread is the range of accepted discrepancies, or NA when there is no comparison. See R/sem-optim.R.

nonlinear <- fit_sem(paste(base, "a*b > 0.01", sep = "\n"),
                     mediation_demo)
nonlinear@diagnostics$optimum[c("n_starts", "n_accepted", "best_of",
                                "certified", "spread", "status")]

Factors and the native engine’s gate (0.11.0)

What: Factor, character, and logical covariates on the right side of native regressions expand to reference-coded 0/1 columns before missing rows are removed. fixed_x can fix all dummies; mbco_sem() retains their map across refits. Ordered factors, a categorical treatment or mediator, a label on the whole factor, and a product of two factors are refused. Why: The explicit dummies keep the covariance model and refits consistent. The native engine is now a supported public interface with a frozen syntax and API contract. See R/sem-fit.R and the factor model guide.

d <- transform(mediation_demo,
               group = cut(covariate1, c(-Inf, 0, Inf), labels = c("low", "high")))
fit <- fit_sem(paste("mediator1 ~ a*treatment + group",
                     "outcome ~ b*mediator1 + cp*treatment + group", sep = "\n"), d)
head(fit@table)

What: For nonlinear constraints, the solver now floors variances that occur in the constraint relative to their natural units, adds the unconstrained fit and sign-flipped copies as starts, and will not replace a feasible reference with a worse accepted point. A single accepted start warns. Why: A solver could previously stop on the wrong sign branch or step to an invalid variance. Other fits keep their previous optimization path. See R/sem-optim.R.

gated <- fit_sem(paste(base, "cp == a*b", sep = "\n"), mediation_demo)
gated@diagnostics[c("decrement", "sign_check", "optimum")]

Other 0.11.0 changes include population-average four-way SEs when options(medfit.covariate_mean_variance = TRUE), a moment-based fallback start, development-S7 load compatibility, and refusal to compare AIC/BIC across different observed variable sets. The worked GPA example provides independent numerical comparisons.

How robustness is checked

The four layers inspect different failure modes; they are development tests, not user-facing switches. The optimizer plan describes the design, while the current tests and tests/sim/gates.csv record later implementation. Metamorphic tests change units, row order, syntax order, redundant constraints, and starts and check the corresponding invariant. nloptr fault injection supplies bad statuses, nonfinite or inconsistent output, and thrown errors to test rejection and retries. An edge-case grid exercises near-singularity, bounds, rank, and extreme scales. A seeded randomized sweep compares 180 cases with independent OLS or profile oracles. Its recorded baseline, in correct/refused/flagged/wrong order, is:

Family Correct Refused Flagged Wrong
A 53 0 7 0
B 60 0 0 0
C 17 0 43 0

“Flagged” means an explicit warning or optimum diagnostic, not an independent proof of correctness. The sweep is an expensive development gate; this short example inspects one fit’s user-visible verdict:

fit <- fit_sem(base, mediation_demo)
fit@diagnostics$optimum$status
